category_title: Quietly on-task students who struggle with independent inquiry and rely on peer cues
minimal_context: The student is completing an independent worksheet during the ecology unit.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please complete the independent work for our ecology unit. Read the text and answer the questions on your worksheet.

STUDENT: (Nods and looks down at the worksheet, quietly taking notes on the inquiry activity.)

TUTOR: Are you making progress on the questions?

STUDENT: (Continues to work independently with minimal interaction, opening a new tab on the Internet to search for the answer rather than raising a hand.)

TUTOR: Keep trying to find the answers on your own.

STUDENT: (Glances over at the student sitting next to him) When I need help, I would just guess or see if I would try and figure it out. Mostly I looked for what other people were doing. That’s how I completed my work.

options.A: Ask questions that encourage the student to share their views and make connections, such as 'Do animals have feelings?'
options.B: Utilize visual supports, including videos and graphs, and provide task initiation supports for the worksheet.
options.C: Demonstrate understanding and provide a couple of more days of flexibility with the worksheet deadline.
options.D: Agree with the student that they are having a rough time with the ecology worksheet.
